title: The singular suffix pronouns on names

blocks.text: My book is a suffix attached to the name. You've known him since ⁧اِسْمِي⁩ , ⁧حَالُكَ⁩ , ⁧عِنْدَهُ⁩ ; Now you study it systematically, with its rules of handwriting and pronunciation, and use it to talk about the family. You will also learn the words of kinship, including the distinction between paternal and maternal uncles that Italian does not make.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 25 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-09), script for speech synthesis, family photos (your or invented)
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. attack the suffixes -ī, -ka, -ki, -hu, -hā in any name, even with ⁧ة⁩ ;
2. use the case vowel before the suffix and pass -hu → -hi;
3. accord the adjective with a name with a suffix ( ⁧بَيْتُهُ الكَبِيرُ⁩ );
4. use special forms of ⁧أَب⁩ and ⁧أَخ⁩ ;
5. appoint family members and describe a family tree;
6. Talk about your family for a minute.
Plan of the week.

What to notice. ⁧اسْمُهُ⁩ His name is his, ⁧اسْمُهَا⁩ The same word with two suffixes. After ⁧مَعَ⁩ the name with suffix is to the genitive: . ⁧مَعَ زَوْجِهَا⁩ In ⁧وَابْنِهَا⁩ the alif ⁧اِبْن⁩ è waṣla: wa-bnihā . ⁧أَخِي الصَّغِيرُ⁩ My younger brother has the adjective with the article, because the name with suffix is determined (A1-04).
She ⁧ـهَا⁩ -hā ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ kitābuhā ⁧سَيَّارَتُهَا⁩ sayyāratuhā your... (of her)

The suffix indicates the owner, not the possessed thing. In Italian  "his" does not say whether the owner is a man or a woman; in Arabic yes: ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ is the book of him, ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ The book of her. The kind of book doesn't count. The name with suffix is determined: no article, nothing tanwīn (A1-04).
1) ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ . In front of any suffix tāʾ marbūṭa opens in tāʾ: ⁧سَيَّارَة⁩ → ⁧سَيَّارَتِي⁩ , ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ → ⁧مَدِينَتُهَا⁩ ,
⁧عَائِلَة⁩ → ⁧عَائِلَتُكَ⁩ . It is always pronounced t .
2) The vowel of the case is before the suffix. The name holds his desinence: -u to the name, -a to the accused,
- I'm in the genitive. In front of the suffix there is no tanwīn.

blocks.text: With -ī The voice of the case is not heard: ⁧كِتَابِي⁩ It's the same in all cases.

3) -hu becomes -hi after i, ī or ay, so also to the genitive: ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِ⁩ fī baytihi ... in his house... ⁧مَعَ أَخِيهِ⁩ With her Brother ⁧عَلَيْهِ⁩ On him. The pronunciation follows the previous vowel: it is a vocal harmony, not a different case. The adjective after a name with suffix takes the article and case of the name: ⁧بَيْتُهُ الجَدِيدُ⁩ His new house is in the middle of the world. ⁧فِي بَيْتِهِ الجَدِيدِ⁩ In his new house. Without an article it becomes preached: ⁧بَيْتُهُ جَدِيدٌ⁩ His house is new.
"Father" and "brother" when they have a suffix (other than -ī) or another name later, lengthen the appropriate vowel:
Accused ⁧أَبَاكَأَبِي⁩ abāka ⁧أَبَاهُ⁩ abāhu ⁧أَبَاهَا⁩ abāhā

⁧أَخ⁩ It works the same way: ⁧أَخِي⁩ , ⁧أَخُوكَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ أَخِيهِ⁩ . Even in front of a name: ⁧أَخُو أَبِي⁩ "My father's brother" ⁧فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي سَلْمَى⁩ At the home of the father of Salmā». In practice. For A1 use safely ⁧أَبِي⁩ / ⁧أَخِي⁩ and the shape of the name ( ⁧أَبُوكَ⁩ , ⁧أَخُوهُ⁩ ); the others recognize them. In standard Arabic they are often used also ⁧وَالِد⁩ wālid "Father" ⁧وَالِدَة⁩ wālida "Mother' is the name of the family. ⁧الوَالِدَانِ⁩ The parents who have regular forms: ⁧وَالِدُكَ⁩ , ⁧مَعَ وَالِدِهِ⁩ .

Because two "zii" are. In traditional Arabic societies, the father's and mother's families have different roles, and the language always distinguishes them. In a conversation, my uncle requires a choice: ⁧عَمِّي⁩ or ⁧خَالِي⁩ . Names in person. In the chain of the name, "son" is written without aliph between two names: ⁧مُحَمَّد بْن عَلِيّ⁩ Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (you often read bin). Many adults are called with the kunya, the father of / mother of the child + the name of the first child: ⁧أَبُو أَحْمَد⁩ Abū Aḥmad , ⁧أُمُّ يُوسُف⁩ Umm Yūsuf . It is a loving and respectful use. The complete structure of the Arabic name (ism, nasab, kunya, laqab, nisba) you will study it in A2.

-ka, -ki, -hu, -hā They don't eat. In the pause, the disappearance of the case falls, but the suffix remains whole: kitābuka , kitābuki . In the quick talk and dialects they become -ak , -ik , -u , -ha: recognize them, but in full pronunciation MSA. The t of ⁧ة⁩ . sayyāratī , madīnatuhā : the t is clearly heard. ⁧ع⁩ in ⁧عَمّ⁩ , ⁧خ⁩ in ⁧خَال⁩ . ʿamm (ʿayn + double m) and ḫāl (ḫāʾ scraped): two sounds that distinguish two relatives. The šadda. ⁧جَدّ⁩ ǧadd , ⁧عَمّ⁩ ʿamm , ⁧أُمّ⁩ umm: the final double consonant can be heard especially with the suffix: ⁧جَدِّي⁩ ǧaddī , ⁧عَمِّي⁩ ʿammī , ⁧أُمِّي⁩ ummī .
⁧كُنْيَة⁩ kunya nickname of the father / mother of the mother of the child ⁧ك ن ي⁩ name f.
⁧ضَمِير⁩ ḍamīr pronoun; consciousness ⁧ض م ر⁩ grammatical term pl. ⁧ضَمَائِر⁩ ḍamāʾir

Notes of use. ⁧إِخْوَة⁩ is the plural of ⁧أَخ⁩ which often includes brothers and sisters; for brothers in a figurative sense (religious, political) use ⁧إِخْوَان⁩ iḫwān . ⁧اِبْن⁩ loses the aliif between two own names ( ⁧بْن⁩ ). ⁧أَعْزَب⁩ has an irregular female, such as color adjectives (A1-03). ⁧أُسْرَة⁩ is the restricted family (parents and children), ⁧عَائِلَة⁩ the family in a broad sense; overlap in use.
